newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Highlands says Q1 hit by higher costs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Highlands says Q1 hit by higher costs.

text.p: Highlands Gold Ltd said on Tuesday its lower first quarter net profit was due to higher operating costs, lower gold output and increased exchange losses due to the currency translation of U.S. dollar borrowings.
Highlands said these factors were partially offset by reduced exploration expenditure and a lower income tax charge.
Earlier Highlands reported a net profit of 2.54 million Papua New Guinea (PNG) kina for the three months ended September 30, 1996, compared with 6.96 million kina a year earlier.
It said at September 30, it had sold forward 412,600 ounces of gold at an average maturity of US$427 per ounce.
Highlands said its forward hedge contracts expire in June 2002.

The gold miner said its share of gold output from its 25 percent interest in the giant Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea fell to 53,390 ounces of gold in the September quarter from 70,297 ounces in the September quarter of 1995.
Porgera is Highland's only current gold production interest.
